_comment: WindowsGSH Steam module manifest template. Keep this file named module.json. Unknown fields like _comment are ignored by WindowsGSH.
_comment_id: Required. Lowercase unique module id. Used for folder names and server moduleId. Example: my-survival-game.
name: Blank Steam Template Server
_comment_name: Required. Friendly name shown in the UI.
author: Your Name
_comment_author: Shown in Module Management. Replace with your name or organisation.
description: Template WindowsGSH module for a SteamCMD dedicated server.
_comment_description: Shown in Module Management. Keep this short and useful.
_comment_url: Primary link shown in Module Management.
_comment_color: Hex accent colour used behind author.png in Module Management.
_comment_type: Use csharp when shipping a .cs file. Use json for manifest-only modules with no custom C# code.
_comment_entry: Required for C# modules. Fully-qualified public class name implementing IGameServerModule.

steam._comment: Optional. Remove this whole object for non-Steam servers.
steam._comment_appId: Replace with the real Steam dedicated server App ID, for example 258550 for Rust.
steam._comment_anonymous: true for servers that allow anonymous SteamCMD login. false if a Steam account is required to download.
steam._comment_customArguments: Optional privileged SteamCMD option tokens using Windows command-line quoting. SteamCMD +commands are rejected; use dedicated manifest fields instead.

entryPoints._comment: Required. start is the server executable path relative to the server install folder.
entryPoints._comment_processName: Name of the running process without extension. WindowsGSH uses this to detect if the server is already running. Defaults to the start filename without extension.

runtime._comment_consoleStrategy: How WindowsGSH interacts with the server console. Options: Redirected (stdin/stdout, correct for most Steam servers), WindowMessage (custom window-message implementation in C#), RconPreferred (use RCON for commands instead of stdin), LogTailOnly (show logs but no command input), None (no console surface at all).
runtime._comment_portIncrements: How many ports one server instance occupies. WindowsGSH uses this to suggest the next available port when adding a new server.
runtime._comment_defaultArguments: Launch arguments. {key} placeholders are replaced with values from configFields before the server starts.
runtime._comment_logPath: Optional. Log folder path relative to the server install folder, for example logs. WindowsGSH reads this for log display and crash diagnostics.

capabilities._comment_directConnection: true if players connect directly to an IP and port rather than through a relay or matchmaking service.
capabilities._comment_consoleCommands: Set to true only when consoleStrategy is WindowMessage and the C# module implements IModuleConsoleCommandCapability. Leave false for all other strategies.

configFields._comment: configFields define the settings UI shown in WindowsGSH. Values are stored in ServerConfig.json under the settings key and passed to the C# module.
configFields.label: Server Name
configFields.description: Name shown in WindowsGSH and, if your module writes config files, in the game server.

configFields.label: Server IP
configFields.description: Use 0.0.0.0 to bind to all interfaces.

configFields.label: Query Port
configFields._comment_defaultValue: Deliberately no defaultValue here, not a number matching network.port - see the ports[] query entry below for why: a shared default would make this indistinguishable from 'not really a separate port,' and a distinct default would make WindowsGSH open an extra firewall hole for a port nothing is listening on by default. Leave this blank unless your game genuinely answers queries on a different port.
configFields.description: Optional. Only set this if your server answers queries on a different port from the game port.

configFields.label: RCON Password
configFields.description: Optional. Only used if your C# module implements ExecuteRconCommandAsync and sets supportsRcon: true.

configFields.label: Game Mode
configFields._comment: Select fields show a dropdown. Options lists the allowed values.

configFields.label: Additional Arguments
configFields.description: Optional extra launch arguments appended to the command line.

_comment_advanced_fields: Advanced configField options: group (string, groups fields visually in the UI), restartRequired (bool, flags that a server restart is needed after the value changes), validationPattern (regex string), validationMessage (shown when the pattern fails), visibleWhen.key + visibleWhen.equals or visibleWhen.isTruthy (hide/show a field based on another field value).

ports._comment: Ports declare the server's network surface for Server Doctor, firewall diagnostics, and manual port-forwarding instructions. Each port must set exactly one of configField, fixedValue, or offsetFrom.
ports.name: Game Port
ports._comment_configField: Reads the effective port from a configField's value at runtime. Must reference a real configFields key.

ports.name: Query Port
ports._comment_query: Not required, and network.queryPort has no default above - a fresh server leaves this port Unresolved (not Invalid, not overlapping the game port) until someone fills in a real value. Only remove this entry if your game can never answer queries on a distinct port at all; leave it declared-but-empty otherwise, since Server Doctor/firewall diagnostics can only ever know about a port that's actually declared here, however it currently resolves.

ports.name: RCON
ports._comment_fixedValue: A literal port number, for a port with no corresponding configField.
ports._comment_openExternally: false marks a port as local-only - it will not be recommended for firewall/UPnP forwarding or manual port-forwarding instructions. Remove this whole rcon entry if your module has no RCON port.

_comment_ports_offset: A port can also be declared relative to another: { "id": "web", "name": "Web Admin", "protocol": "tcp", "offsetFrom": "game", "offset": 1 } resolves to the game port's value plus 1. rangeSize (default 1) reserves that many consecutive ports starting at the resolved value, for servers that occupy a block of ports.

backupTargets._comment: Backup targets appear on the Backups tab. Paths are relative to the server install folder.
backupTargets.label: Config

addons._comment: Optional. Remove addons if the server has no addon or mod support. Each entry appears in the Addons tab.
addons.name: Example Addon
addons.description: Shows how addon metadata appears in WindowsGSH.
addons.installInstructions: Download the addon and place it in the server addons folder.

package._comment: Optional automation. Remove this block to keep a manual download-page addon. Supported kinds: Zip, Tar, TarGz, File.
package._comment_expectedSha256: Strongly recommended. SHA-256 of the downloaded archive/file (uppercase or lowercase, case-insensitive), verified before extraction. Leave blank only if you can't pin a hash yet - WindowsGSH will flag it as a module diagnostics warning and install without verifying the download.
